sanskrit: tataḥ prakṣālanaṃ kṛtvā samadhiśritya bāhukaḥ tṛṇamuṣṭiṃ samādāya āvidhyainaṃ samādadhat
english: Then, having washed his hands and approached the hearth, Bahuka took up a handful of grass, swung it around, and placed it upon the fire.

sanskrit: atha prajvalitas tatra sahasā havyavāhanaḥ tad adbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāham ihāgatā
english: Thereupon the fire-carrier blazed up suddenly in that place; marvelling at that most wondrous sight, I came here astonished.

sanskrit: anyac ca tasmin sumahad āścaryaṃ lakṣitaṃ mayā yad agnim api saṃspṛśya naiva dahyaty asau śubhe
english: And another great wonder was observed by me there, O fair one: that even on touching the fire he is not burnt at all.

sanskrit: chandena codakaṃ tasya vahaty āvarjitaṃ drutam atīva cānyat sumahad āścaryaṃ dṛṣṭavaty aham
english: Water rises up to him willingly and swiftly by his mere wish; and yet another exceedingly great wonder have I witnessed.

sanskrit: yat sa puṣpāṇy upādāya hastābhyāṃ mamṛde śanaiḥ mṛdyamānāni pāṇibhyāṃ tena puṣpāṇi tāny atha
english: That taking up flowers and crushing them gently in both his hands — those flowers crushed thus in his palms —

sanskrit: bhūya eva sugandhīni hṛṣitāni bhavanti ca etāny adbhutakalpāni dṛṣṭvāhaṃ drutam āgatā
english: became all the more fragrant and bloomed afresh. Having seen these things that are near to miracles, I came running here.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca damayantī tu tac chrutvā puṇyaślokasya ceṣṭitam amanyata nalaṃ prāptaṃ karmaceṣṭābhisūcitam
english: Brihadashva said: Having heard this account of the deeds of the illustrious Nala, Damayanti concluded that Nala had been found, indicated by those acts and movements.

sanskrit: sā śaṅkamānā bhartāraṃ nalaṃ bāhukarūpiṇam keśinīṃ ślakṣṇayā vācā rudatī punar abravīt
english: Suspecting that her husband Nala was concealed in the form of Bahuka, she again spoke to Keshini, weeping, in a gentle voice.

sanskrit: punar gaccha pramattasya bāhukasyopasaṃskṛtam mahānasāc chṛtaṃ māṃsaṃ samādāyaihi bhāmini
english: "Go again, O fair one, and while Bahuka is unaware, take the cooked meat that has been prepared by him from the kitchen and bring it here."

sanskrit: sā gatvā bāhuke vyagre tan māṃsam apakṛṣya ca atyuṣṇam eva tvaritā tatkṣaṇaṃ priyakāriṇī damayantyai tataḥ prādāt keśinī kurunandana
english: She went, and while Bahuka was occupied, drew away that meat, still piping hot; then swiftly, the ever-obliging Keshini at that very moment gave it to Damayanti, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: socitā nalasiddhasya māṃsasya bahuśaḥ purā prāśya matvā nalaṃ sūdaṃ prākrośad bhṛśaduḥkhitā
english: She who had long been accustomed to the cooking of Nala tasted that meat and, recognising Nala in the cook, cried out in great grief.

sanskrit: vaiklavyaṃ ca paraṃ gatvā prakṣālya ca mukhaṃ tataḥ mithunaṃ preṣayām āsa keśinyā saha bhārata
english: And overcome with extreme anguish, she washed her face, then sent the pair of children together with Keshini, O Bharata.

sanskrit: indrasenāṃ saha bhrātrā samabhijñāya bāhukaḥ abhidrutya tato rājā pariṣvajyāṅkam ānayat
english: Recognising Indrasena together with her brother, Bahuka the king rushed forward and, embracing them, drew them into his lap.

sanskrit: bāhukas tu samāsādya sutau surasutopamau bhṛśaṃ duḥkhaparītātmā sasvaraṃ prarudoda ha
english: But Bahuka, approaching his two children who were like the children of gods, his heart overwhelmed with deep grief, wept aloud.

sanskrit: naiṣadho darśayitvā tu vikāram asakṛt tadā utsṛjya sahasā putrau keśinīm idam abravīt
english: The king of Nishadha, having shown his agitation more than once, then quickly let go of his children and said this to Keshini:

sanskrit: idaṃ susadṛśaṃ bhadre mithunaṃ mama putrayoḥ tato dṛṣṭvaiva sahasā bāṣpam utsṛṣṭavān aham
english: "This pair, O good woman, is very similar to my own children; that is why on merely seeing them I immediately shed tears."

sanskrit: bahuśaḥ saṃpatantīṃ tvāṃ janaḥ śaṅketa doṣataḥ vayaṃ ca deśātithayo gaccha bhadre namo 'stu te
english: "People seeing you come here so many times might suspect some fault. We too are but guests in this land — go, O good woman, I salute you."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sarvaṃ vikāraṃ dṛṣṭvā tu puṇyaślokasya dhīmataḥ āgatya keśinī kṣipraṃ damayantyai nyavedayat
english: Brihadashva said: Having observed all the emotions of the wise and illustrious Nala, Keshini came quickly and reported everything to Damayanti.

sanskrit: damayantī tato bhūyaḥ preṣayām āsa keśinīm mātuḥ sakāśaṃ duḥkhārtā nalaśaṅkāsamutsukā
english: Then Damayanti, afflicted with sorrow and agitated by her suspicion that it was Nala, sent Keshini once more to her mother.

sanskrit: parīkṣito me bahuśo bāhuko nalaśaṅkayā rūpe me saṃśayas tv ekaḥ svayam icchāmi veditum
english: "Bahuka has been tested by me many times on suspicion that he is Nala; I have one single doubt about his form — I wish to know it myself."

sanskrit: sa vā praveśyatāṃ mātar māṃ vānujñātum arhasi viditaṃ vātha vājñātaṃ pitur me saṃvidhīyatām
english: "Either let him be brought in to me, mother, or you should give me leave to go; whether it be known or unknown, let my father arrange it."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu vaidarbhyā sā devī bhīmam abravīt duhitus tam abhiprāyam anvajānāc ca pārthivaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, that queen spoke to Bhima, and the king assented to his daughter's intention.

sanskrit: sā vai pitrābhyanujñātā mātrā ca bharatarṣabha nalaṃ praveśayām āsa yatra tasyāḥ pratiśrayaḥ
english: Permitted thus by her father and mother, O bull of the Bharatas, she brought Nala in to the place where her own quarters were.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathāyuktaṃ damayantī nalaṃ tadā tīvraśokasamāviṣṭā babhūva varavarṇinī
english: But seeing Nala arrived in that form, Damayanti of excellent complexion was then seized by sharp grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāṣāyavasanā jaṭilā malapaṅkinī damayantī mahārāja bāhukaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Damayanti, clad in ochre garments, matted-haired and begrimed with dirt, O great king, spoke these words to Bahuka:

sanskrit: dṛṣṭapūrvas tvayā kaś cid dharmajño nāma bāhuka suptām utsṛjya vipine gato yaḥ puruṣaḥ striyam
english: "Have you ever seen, Bahuka, a man who knows the law, one who abandoned a sleeping woman in the forest and went away?"

sanskrit: anāgasaṃ priyāṃ bhāryāṃ vijane śramamohitām apahāya tu ko gacchet puṇyaślokam ṛte nalam
english: "Who but Nala of celebrated fame could abandon in a lonely place, exhausted and stupefied with fatigue, a beloved wife who had committed no offence?"

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tasya mayā kāryam aparāddhaṃ mahīpateḥ yo mām utsṛjya vipine gatavān nidrayā hṛtām
english: "What wrong was done to him by me, that lord of the earth, who went away leaving me in the forest, carried off by sleep?"

sanskrit: sākṣād devān apāhāya vṛto yaḥ sa mayā purā anuvratāṃ sābhikāmāṃ putriṇīṃ tyaktavān katham
english: "How could he have abandoned me, who was devoted to him, who desired him above all, who was then a mother — me, whom of old I chose setting aside the gods themselves?"

sanskrit: agnau pāṇigṛhītāṃ ca haṃsānāṃ vacane sthitām bhariṣyāmīti satyaṃ ca pratiśrutya kva tad gatam
english: "Where has that truth gone — the promise he swore: 'I will provide for you' — made when he took my hand in the fire, when he trusted the words of the swans?"

sanskrit: damayantyā bruvantyās tu sarvam etad ariṃdama śokajaṃ vāri netrābhyām asukhaṃ prāsravad bahu
english: As Damayanti spoke all this, O subduer of enemies, tears born of grief flowed copiously and unhappily from both her eyes.

sanskrit: atīva kṛṣṇatārābhyāṃ raktāntābhyāṃ jalaṃ tu tat parisravan nalo dṛṣṭvā śokārta idam abravīt
english: Seeing those tears flowing from her dark-pupilled, red-cornered eyes, Nala, distressed with grief, spoke thus:

sanskrit: mama rājyaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ yan nāhaṃ tat kṛtavān svayam kalinā tat kṛtaṃ bhīru yac ca tvām aham atyajam
english: "My kingdom was destroyed — yet that was not done by me of my own will; it was done by Kali, O timid one, and so too was my abandoning of you."

sanskrit: tvayā tu dharmabhṛcchreṣṭhe śāpenābhihataḥ purā vanasthayā duḥkhitayā śocantyā māṃ vivāsasam
english: "And by you, O best upholder of dharma, was Kali then struck with a curse — by you who were in the forest, wretched and mourning me who had been exiled."

sanskrit: sa maccharīre tvacchāpād dahyamāno 'vasat kaliḥ tvacchāpadagdhaḥ satataṃ so 'gnāv iva samāhitaḥ
english: "Scorched by your curse, Kali dwelt within my body burning; burnt by your curse constantly, he was like one fixed in fire."

sanskrit: mama ca vyavasāyena tapasā caiva nirjitaḥ duḥkhasyāntena cānena bhavitavyaṃ hi nau śubhe
english: "And he was conquered by my resolution and by ascetic endurance as well; and with this ending of sorrow, O fair one, there must now be happiness for us two."

sanskrit: vimucya māṃ gataḥ pāpaḥ sa tato 'ham ihāgataḥ tvadarthaṃ vipulaśroṇi na hi me 'nyat prayojanam
english: "That wretch has released me and gone; then I came here, O broad-hipped one, for your sake — I have no other purpose here."

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu nārī bhartāram anuraktam anuvratam utsṛjya varayed anyaṃ yathā tvaṃ bhīru karhi cit
english: "How could a woman ever forsake a husband devoted and faithful to her and choose another, as you, O timid one, are alleged to have done?"

sanskrit: dūtāś caranti pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ nṛpatiśāsanāt bhaimī kila sma bhartāraṃ dvitīyaṃ varayiṣyati
english: "Messengers roam the whole earth by order of a king: it is said that Bhima's daughter is about to choose a second husband."

sanskrit: svairavṛttā yathākāmam anurūpam ivātmanaḥ śrutvaiva caivaṃ tvarito bhāṅgasvarir upasthitaḥ
english: "As one acting wantonly according to her own desire, as if suited to herself — having heard this very thing, Rituparna, son of Bhangasvara, arrived hastily."

sanskrit: damayantī tu tac chrutvā nalasya paridevitam prāñjalir vepamānā ca bhītā vacanam abravīt
english: But Damayanti, hearing that lamentation of Nala, trembling and frightened, spoke with joined palms.

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca na mām arhasi kalyāṇa pāpena pariśaṅkitum mayā hi devān utsṛjya vṛtas tvaṃ niṣadhādhipa
english: Damayanti said: You must not, O noble one, suspect me of wrongdoing; for it was I who chose you setting aside the gods themselves, O lord of Nishadha.

sanskrit: tavābhigamanārthaṃ tu sarvato brāhmaṇā gatāḥ vākyāni mama gāthābhir gāyamānā diśo daśa
english: For the purpose of finding you, brahmins went in all directions, singing my words in verse throughout the ten quarters.

sanskrit: tatas tvāṃ brāhmaṇo vidvān parṇādo nāma pārthiva abhyagacchat kosalāyām ṛtuparṇaniveśane
english: Then a learned brahmin named Parnada, O king, came upon you in the abode of Rituparna in Kosala.

sanskrit: tena vākye hṛte samyak prativākye tathāhṛte upāyo 'yaṃ mayā dṛṣṭo naiṣadhānayane tava
english: When the message was duly conveyed by him and the reply likewise received, this stratagem was devised by me for bringing you back, O lord of Nishadha.

sanskrit: tvām ṛte na hi loke 'nya ekāhnā pṛthivīpate samartho yojanaśataṃ gantum aśvair narādhipa
english: "For there is no other in the world, O lord of the earth, O lord of men, capable of covering a hundred yojanas in a single day with horses — none but you."

sanskrit: tathā cemau mahīpāla bhaje 'haṃ caraṇau tava yathā nāsatkṛtaṃ kiṃ cin manasāpi carāmy aham
english: "And so, O ruler of the earth, I clasp your feet in the same way as I have never committed any wrong even in my mind."

sanskrit: ayaṃ carati loke 'smin bhūtasākṣī sadāgatiḥ eṣa muñcatu me prāṇān yadi pāpaṃ carāmy aham
english: "This wind that moves in this world, witness to all beings and ever present — let it take my life if I am guilty of any sin."

sanskrit: tathā carati tigmāṃśuḥ pareṇa bhuvanaṃ sadā sa vimuñcatu me prāṇān yadi pāpaṃ carāmy aham
english: "Likewise the fierce-rayed sun that always moves beyond this world — let it take my life if I am guilty of any sin."

sanskrit: candramāḥ sarvabhūtānām antaś carati sākṣivat sa vimuñcatu me prāṇān yadi pāpaṃ carāmy aham
english: "The moon that moves within all beings as their inner witness — let it take my life if I am guilty of any sin."

sanskrit: ete devās trayaḥ kṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ dhārayanti vai vibruvantu yathāsatyam ete vādya tyajantu mām
english: "These three gods indeed uphold the entire triple world; let them declare what is true, and today let them forsake me if I have sinned."

sanskrit: evam ukte tato vāyur antarikṣād abhāṣata naiṣā kṛtavatī pāpaṃ nala satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: When she had spoken thus, the wind then spoke from the sky: "She has not committed any sin, Nala — I speak the truth to you."

sanskrit: rājañ śīlanidhiḥ sphīto damayantyā surakṣitaḥ sākṣiṇo rakṣiṇaś cāsyā vayaṃ trīn parivatsarān
english: "O king, the great treasure-house of her virtue has been well guarded by Damayanti; we have been her witnesses and protectors for three full years."

sanskrit: upāyo vihitaś cāyaṃ tvadartham atulo 'nayā na hy ekāhnā śataṃ gantā tvad ṛte 'nyaḥ pumān iha
english: "And this unequalled stratagem was devised by her for your sake; for there is no other man here who could travel a hundred yojanas in a single day but you."

sanskrit: upapannā tvayā bhaimī tvaṃ ca bhaimyā mahīpate nātra śaṅkā tvayā kāryā saṃgaccha saha bhāryayā
english: "Bhima's daughter is worthy of you, and you are worthy of Bhima's daughter, O lord of the earth; you must entertain no doubt here — come together with your wife."

sanskrit: tathā bruvati vāyau tu puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papāta ha devadundubhayo nedur vavau ca pavanaḥ śivaḥ
english: As the wind spoke thus, a shower of flowers fell; the divine kettledrums resounded, and an auspicious breeze blew.

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā nalo rājātha bhārata damayantyāṃ viśaṅkāṃ tāṃ vyapākarṣad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Seeing that most wondrous event, O Bharata, Nala the king, that subduer of enemies, then cast away his suspicion regarding Damayanti.

sanskrit: tatas tad vastram arajaḥ prāvṛṇod vasudhādhipaḥ saṃsmṛtya nāgarājānaṃ tato lebhe vapuḥ svakam
english: Then the lord of the earth put on that spotless garment; calling the king of the serpents to mind, he then regained his own form.

sanskrit: svarūpiṇaṃ tu bhartāraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasutā tadā prākrośad uccair āliṅgya puṇyaślokam aninditā
english: Seeing her husband in his own form, the blameless daughter of Bhima then cried out loudly, embracing the illustrious Nala.

sanskrit: bhaimīm api nalo rājā bhrājamāno yathā purā sasvaje svasutau cāpi yathāvat pratyanandata
english: King Nala too embraced Bhima's daughter, radiant as before; and he greeted his own children duly as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ svorasi vinyasya vaktraṃ tasya śubhānanā parītā tena duḥkhena niśaśvāsāyatekṣaṇā
english: Then, burying her lovely face upon his chest, overwhelmed by that accumulated grief, she of beautiful eyes sighed deeply.

sanskrit: tathaiva maladigdhāṅgī pariṣvajya śucismitā suciraṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ tasthau sāśrupariplutā
english: Just so, her limbs still begrimed with dirt, the pure-smiled one stood clinging to that tiger among men for a long time, her eyes flooded with tears.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ damayantyā nalasya ca bhīmāyākathayat prītyā vaidarbhyā jananī nṛpa
english: Then Damayanti's mother joyfully told Bhima everything that had occurred concerning Damayanti and Nala, O king.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahārājaḥ kṛtaśaucam ahaṃ nalam damayantyā sahopetaṃ kālyaṃ draṣṭā sukhoṣitam
english: Then the great king said: "Tomorrow I shall see Nala, who has bathed and purified himself, dwelling happily together with Damayanti."

sanskrit: tatas tau sahitau rātriṃ kathayantau purātanam vane vicaritaṃ sarvam ūṣatur muditau nṛpa
english: Then those two, together through the night, narrating all the former tale of their wandering in the forest, passed the night joyfully, O king.

sanskrit: sa caturthe tato varṣe saṃgamya saha bhāryayā sarvakāmaiḥ susiddhārtho labdhavān paramāṃ mudam
english: And he, meeting again with his wife in that fourth year, all his wishes fully accomplished, attained supreme joy.

sanskrit: damayanty api bhartāram avāpyāpyāyitā bhṛśam ardhasaṃjātasasyeva toyaṃ prāpya vasuṃdharā
english: And Damayanti too, having regained her husband, was greatly refreshed — like the earth receiving rain when the crops are half-grown.

sanskrit: saivaṃ sametya vyapanītatandrī; śāntajvarā harṣavivṛddhasattvā rarāja bhaimī samavāptakāmā; śītāṃśunā rātrir ivoditena
english: She thus reunited, her weariness dispelled, her fever stilled, her spirit swelling with joy — Bhima's daughter shone in her fulfilled desire like the night risen with the cool-rayed moon.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca atha tāṃ vyuṣito rātriṃ nalo rājā svalaṃkṛtaḥ vaidarbhyā sahitaḥ kālyaṃ dadarśa vasudhādhipam
english: Brihadashva said: Having passed that night there, King Nala, well adorned and accompanied by the princess of Vidarbha, presented himself at dawn before the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādayām āsa prayataḥ śvaśuraṃ nalaḥ tasyānu damayantī ca vavande pitaraṃ śubhā
english: Then Nala, with due reverence, saluted his father-in-law; and after him, the fair Damayanti bowed to her father.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaḥ pratijagrāha putravat parayā mudā yathārhaṃ pūjayitvā tu samāśvāsayata prabhuḥ nalena sahitāṃ tatra damayantīṃ pativratām
english: Bhima received him with great joy as if he were a son; having honoured him fittingly, the lord consoled Damayanti, devoted to her husband, there together with Nala.

sanskrit: tām arhaṇāṃ nalo rājā pratigṛhya yathāvidhi paricaryāṃ svakāṃ tasmai yathāvat pratyavedayat
english: King Nala received that honourable gift according to due rite and duly reported to him his own service rendered.

sanskrit: tato babhūva nagare sumahān harṣanisvanaḥ janasya saṃprahṛṣṭasya nalaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatam
english: Then in the city arose a very great sound of jubilation from the people, delighted to see Nala returned in such a manner.

sanskrit: aśobhayac ca nagaraṃ patākādhvajamālinam siktasaṃmṛṣṭapuṣpāḍhyā rājamārgāḥ kṛtās tadā
english: The city was adorned and made beautiful with garlands of banners and flags; the royal roads were sprinkled, swept, and richly strewn with flowers.

sanskrit: dvāri dvāri ca paurāṇāṃ puṣpabhaṅgaḥ prakalpitaḥ arcitāni ca sarvāṇi devatāyatanāni ca
english: At the doorway of every townsman, garlands of flowers were arranged; and all the shrines of the gods were worshipped and adorned.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇo 'pi śuśrāva bāhukacchadminaṃ nalam damayantyā samāyuktaṃ jahṛṣe ca narādhipaḥ
english: Rituparna too heard that Nala, who had been disguised as Bahuka, was united with Damayanti, and the lord of men rejoiced.

sanskrit: tam ānāyya nalo rājā kṣamayām āsa pārthivam sa ca taṃ kṣamayām āsa hetubhir buddhisaṃmataḥ
english: King Nala, summoning him, begged pardon of the king; and that king too begged his pardon with reasons approved by reason.

sanskrit: sa satkṛto mahīpālo naiṣadhaṃ vismayānvitaḥ diṣṭyā sameto dāraiḥ svair bhavān ity abhyanandata
english: That lord of the earth, duly honoured, filled with wonder, congratulated the lord of Nishadha saying: "By good fortune you are reunited with your own wife."

sanskrit: kaccit tu nāparādhaṃ te kṛtavān asmi naiṣadha ajñātavāsaṃ vasato madgṛhe niṣadhādhipa
english: "Have I not done you any wrong, O lord of Nishadha, O ruler of Nishadha, while you dwelt unknown in my house?"

sanskrit: yadi vā buddhipūrvāṇi yady abuddhāni kāni cit mayā kṛtāny akāryāṇi tāni me kṣantum arhasi
english: "Whether done deliberately or unknowingly, whatever improper things were done by me — those you must forgive."
